newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Conservative rebounds in latest Nicaraguan poll.
newsitem.headline: Conservative rebounds in latest Nicaraguan poll.

text.p: Conservative presidential candidate Arnoldo Aleman rebounded in a poll released on Tuesday, extending his lead over former President Daniel Ortega to eight points ahead of Nicaragua's October 20 elections.

The poll by the Costa Rican firm Borge y Asociados gave Liberal Alliance candidate Aleman 42.9 percent of the vote and Ortega of the left-wing Sandinista Front 34.7 percent, followed by a jumble of 22 lesser candidates.
"The poll showed that Arnoldo Aleman is clearly headed for a first round victory," Aleman campaign chief Jorge Salaverry said in an interview.
If the 12.3 percent of undecided voters are removed from the poll, Aleman received 48.2 percent of those polled. He needs 45 percent to avoid a run-off vote with Ortega.
The Borge y Asociados poll was a breath of fresh air for Aleman who had seen Ortega surging in the polls, closing the once double-digit gap between the candidates to almost nothing.
A poll released last week by the Nicaraguan company CINCO S.A. even showed Ortega leading Aleman 33.1 percent to 32.1 percent in the capital Managua.
Pre-election polls in Nicaragua have a history of being wildly inaccurate.

Before Nicaragua's 1990 elections, most polling companies predicted an easy Sandinista victory, giving them 60 percent of the vote. But the Sandinistas lost, as President Violeta Chamorro was swept to power by a wide margin.
Only Borge y Asociados predicted the victory by Chamorro's National Opposition Union (UNO).
Borge y Asociados polled 1,200 Nicaraguans from September 21-23, with a margin of error of five percent.
